correctness.rationale: For each complete multipartite graph with one vacancy, the moving type-c agent removed from full source part i has self-inclusive occupied closed-neighborhood fraction (C_c-n_ic+1)/(V-a_i), exactly the marginal removed from the displayed sum of u_ic(q_ic(h)). Arrival to destination part j makes it full, the added marginal is u_jc((C_c-n_jc)/(V-a_j)); same-part jumps do not change utility. Therefore potential change equals agent utility change for every move, despite arbitrary nonlinear type-and-part payoffs. Only finitely many count matrices exist, proving FIP and the stated m∏(a_i+1)^(k−1)-1 bound. The four claimed strictly improving two-vacancy K3,3 moves with peak p(f)=1−|2f−1| return to the identical labeled state, showing one-vacancy sharpness as a uniform guarantee. An independently constructed rational enumeration confirmed 1,532 move identities across 344 profiles and all four moves of the cycle.

originality.rationale: The original self-inclusive single-peaked Schelling jump-game literature includes cycles and equilibrium results on other graph families, while versions based on neighbor-only fractions or resource selection differ materially in utility denominators and feasible moves. A Rosenthal-style potential resembles the sum of marginal rewards, but the exact reduction of the one-vacancy graph occupancy dynamics is the evaluated contribution. Targeted Resultary search returned no matching implication. General congestion-game exact potential theory is acknowledged as a possible stronger result only if it instantiates this particular jump geometry and self-inclusive fraction.

value.rationale: A complete family-wide finite-improvement theorem for nonmonotone single-peaked and arbitrary heterogeneous utilities, an explicit polynomial trajectory bound for fixed type/part counts, and a four-step sharp multi-vacancy obstruction answer substantive convergence questions in Schelling dynamics. The exact potential reveals why these graph and vacancy restrictions matter.
